section.title: Containers, backups and system areas
section.intro: Virtual machines, backups and parts of macOS that are shown but not offered.

rules.title: iPhone or iPad backup
rules.whatItIs: A backup of an iPhone or iPad stored on this Mac.
rules.consequence: That backup would be gone for good, and if the device is lost with no iCloud backup its data cannot be recovered.
rules.sideCondition: Delete from Finder or the Apple Devices app, not by hand.

rules.title: Docker disk image
rules.whatItIs: The single file holding every Docker image, container and volume.
rules.consequence: Deleting it would destroy all your images, containers and volume data, including databases.
rules.sideCondition: Never remove the file itself. The command clears only unused items.

rules.title: Virtual machine
rules.whatItIs: A virtual machine and everything stored inside it.
rules.consequence: You would lose that virtual machine and all of its data.

rules.title: OS update area
rules.whatItIs: Files macOS uses to stage and apply updates.
rules.consequence: Removing them could interfere with system updates.

rules.title: Swap and sleep files
rules.whatItIs: Memory swap files managed by the system.
rules.consequence: They are managed by macOS and the space returns by itself.
rules.sideCondition: Shown under system volumes, not offered.

rules.title: System temporary data
rules.whatItIs: Temporary files and caches in use by running programs.
rules.consequence: Programs that are running would fail or lose their working data.

rules.title: System logs
rules.whatItIs: Logs and diagnostics macOS keeps for the whole system.
rules.consequence: They belong to macOS and are mostly owned by the system, so they are not offered for removal.

rules.title: App language files
rules.whatItIs: Language files inside an installed app.
rules.consequence: Removing them may invalidate the app's signature so it will not open.
